newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dry weather stops Porgera mill throughput.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dry weather stops Porgera mill throughput.

text.p: The partners of the giant Porgera gold mine in the highlands of Papua New Guinea said recent dry weather had forced the suspension of mill throughput on Sunday.
They said the suspension may affect gold production levels in the month of June if there was no substantial rainfall in the next few days.

The partners are operator Placer Dome Inc with 50 percent, 25 percent shareholder Goldfields Ltd, the PNG government-controlled Orogen Minerals Ltd with 15 percent and the government of Papua New Guinea with 10 percent.

They said the suspension followed several periods of dry weather in the highlands, with the most recent dry spell leading to a serious reduction in water levels at the mine's main water supply, the Waile Creek dam.
While mining and other operations were not affected, mill throughput would be restricted until the main reservoir began to fill.
Essential maintenance that was planned for the processing circuit in June and July would now be brought forward.
The mine produced 232,164 ounces of gold in the first quarter of calendar 1997 and produces in the order of one million ounces eaCh year.
